questions.question:
Laboratory mice inventory list

How many Heterozygous mice are available in the Cardiology and Nephrology labs?
questions.explanation: To answer this question, we need to sum up all the heterozygous mice, both dominant and recessive, in the Cardiology and Nephrology labs. To do that, we need to sum up the numbers appearing in the cell where Nephrology and Cardiology columns cross with the Hetreozygous Dominant and Heterozygous Recessive rows: 9+16+7+11=43. Thus, the answer is B.

questions.question:
Job Prospects for University Graduates

What percentage of private university graduates was unemployed in 2000?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is D. The total number of private university graduates in 2000 = 125 + 1350 = 1,475 The percentage of unemployed graduates in 2000 = (125 /1,475) x 100 = 8.47%

questions.question:
Laboratory mice inventory list

If all knockout mice were transferred from the the neuroscience lab to the pharmacology labs - how many mice would the pharmacology lab have?
questions.explanation: To answer this question, we need to sum up the knockout mice from the Neuroscience lab with all the mice in the Pharmacology lab. To do that, we need to look at the number that appears in the cell where the Neuroscience column cross with the Knockout row, and then add it to the numbers appearing in the Pharmacology column: 5+10+10+3+3=31. Thus, the answer is C.

Imogen has decided to become a working-immigrant in the near-by planet of Poliphilia. She decided to use the long journey through time and space in order to become familiar with the local culture. She decided to check which of Poliphilia's seven states is sure to have the most vacation days during the year. Alas, the Poliphilians, although also having exactly 12 months like Earth, have different measures, which Earth-people can only interpret to colours and estimations.

In which state should Imogen work?

questions.question:
A sportswear store offers various brands of shoes for sale. Each salesperson in the store receives a base salary of 80 USD per workday, and can receive an additional bonus based on sales made. The sum of the bonus will be based on the number, and type of shoes sold (see above chart).

What is the minimal number of Comverse pairs Danny has to sell to be able to skip a day at work?
questions.explanation: Since we know Danny's daily base salary is $80, we can deduce that he has to make a bigger bonus than that in order to be able to skip a day at work. By looking at the table we see that there is a $12 for selling each pair of Comverse shoes. The minimum number of Comverse shoes Danny can sell to cover his daily base salary of $80 is therefore equal to: 80÷12 = 6.67. Note that since Danny cannot sell a fraction of a pair of shoes, we must round up to 7. Thus, the answer is E.

questions.question:
Martin came back from a magnificent trip in the northern territories of Canada. His sheer joy was dimmed only due to the fact that he had forgotten to buy a present to his nephew. Fortunately, he noticed a sign: Forgot to buy a present to your host? Last Minute Gifts - We have them all!

If Martin trades 100 Canadian dollars to British pounds and buys the least cheap Canadian gift from the shop, how much change would he have left after buying a £51 train ticket home?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is E. The calculation is made within 2 steps: 1. Trade 100 Canadian $ (CAD) to £ (GBP) = sum of money X exchange rate = 100 X 0.650 = 65. 2. Subtract the gift's value = 65 – a hat (least cheap Canada made souvenir) = 65-14.4 = 50.6. The outcome is less than 51, the required sum for the train journey, therefore Martin cannot afford the train ticket unless he trades more money. Answer C will be obtained if one decided to buy maple syrup (not the least cheap) as g

questions.question:
Jerald is a 27 years old chap from Liverpool. As a great fan of Scottish beer, he decided to surprise his 22 years old girlfriend Shannon, by taking her on a 3-day road trip to Aberdeen, Scotland, to visit the famous "Smurffie's" brewery. In order to impress Shannon, Jerald has decided to rent the highest-class car he can afford (with class A being the highest), with a limited budget of $200.

What car would you advise Jerald to rent, knowing that he drives only automatic-gear vehicles and that he would probably wish to share the driving with Shannon?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is E. The best solving method would be by a process of elimination. Calculate the maximum possible daily tariff by dividing the budget to three days: 200/3 = 66.667 Eliminate all options that exceed this limit. Afterwards, eliminate options which present vehicles with manual gear (since Jerald cannot drive these) or age limitation of over 21 (since then Shannon wouldn't be able to share driving with Jerald). Only two cars eventually fit the demands – "Fleet", represented by distractor E and "Coconut", represented by the distractor D. Jerald should choose "Fleet", since it is has a higher class rate. Other distractors might send you to some wrong answers: A directs to "Tiger", a convertible that exceeds budget.

Rate of Occupational Growth in the UK (Between the years 1995-2012)

What can be induced from the graph shown above?
choices: Some occupations are not in growth.
There are more psychologists than scientists.
There are similar numbers of teachers and scientists in the UK.
Occupations shown in the graph that demand working directly with people are growing at a faster rate than other occupations.
questions.explanation: To answer this question, we need to decide if each answer option is true or false. Some occupations are not in growth. - False. The numbers shown in the graph are only relative. Examine the chart below and answer the following questions: Nutritional value of yogurt products by five different manufacturers

Which yogurt contains the highest percent of protein of its caloric intake?
questions.explanation: To answer this question, we need to estimate the proportion of protein calories for each yogurt. To do that, we can simply calculate the proportion of protein weight vs caloric intake for each yogurt since we do not know the caloric value for 1 gram of protein: 1. "Tempo": 7/207 =0.034 2. "Cisco": 8/242 = 0.033 3. "Salty": 4.5/189= 0.024 4. "Blanco": 6/220 =0.027 5. "Magic": 7/190 =0.037 Thus, the answer is E.

questions.question:
DETAILS Assume that you are in charge of maintaining the inventory of supplies for the office. The table below describes the current status, and use projections for the next quarter (based on previous quarters), of some supplies in several departments in the office. As you are in charge of maintaining the office's inventory, you must make sure all departments have enough supplies for the upcoming quarter. Note that pencils come in packs of 12, pens come in packs of 3, and paper comes in packs of 5 reams. You should order enough to last the next quarter, but nothing more than necessary. Also note that packs cannot be divided between departments.

Assuming pencils cost $1.20 per pack, how much should the order of pencils for the Management department cost?
questions.explanation: To answer this question, we should first calculate how many units of pencils we need to order. We can do this by using the equation Projected Amount – Current Amount = To-Order Amount (units). Checking for management department's pencils, we see that they are not short of pencils, as there are 4 more pencils than needed: 4 - 8 = -4. Thus, the answer is B.

questions.question:
Movie Tickets

How many children do you need to have in order for a family ticket bought in peak hours to be the cheapest option available, assuming that a family ticket is meant for 2 parents (adults) and their children?
questions.explanation: To answer this question, we need to calculate the cost of individual tickets bought for each family member in peak time and compare it to the price of a family ticket ($32). Let us begin with the smallest family available: 2 Parents + 1 Child: $13 + $13 + $6.75 = 32.75$ >$32 As we can see - a family ticket is the more affordable option even for parents with only one child. Thus, the answer is 1.

One day the store manager decided to triple the bonus for selling Hike shoes. If Danny sold 6 pairs of Hike shoes that day what were his total earnings for the day?
questions.explanation: By looking at the table we can see that the regular bonus for selling Hike shoes is $7. Since we know the bonus was tripled that day, and Danny sold 6 pairs of shoes, we can calculate his daily salary by adding his basic daily salary to the bonus he earned: 6 * 7 * 3 + 80 = 206. Thus, The answer is D.

Selling 8 pairs of A-six and 5 pairs of Hike is equivalent to:
choices: Selling 15 pairs of Adidos and 9 pairs of Scrartchers
Selling 13 pairs of Hike and 11 pairs of Old Balance
Selling 20 pairs of Comverse and 12 pairs of Tiger

questions.question:
Table Sales Report
Percentages reflect the relative amount of tables out of all the items sold that month

The total number of items sold in month 2 was greater than the total number of items sold in month 3.
questions.explanation: In both months the percentage of tables sold (out of all items sold that month) was 20%. However, in month 2, 20% equal 100 tables whereas in month 3 20% equal 50 tables. This means that in month 2 more items were sold compared to month 3. The reason for this is that a percent is a portion of a whole, the more the percent is "worth" in value, the greater the value of the whole. Another way to look at this question: 20% equal 1/5. Month 2: 1/5 of all items equal 100. This means that all items equal 100*5= 500 items. Month 3: 1/5 of all items equal 50. This means that all items equal 50*5= 250 items.

questions.question:
Rate of Occupational Growth in the US
(Between the years 1995-2012)

The number of scientist has not changed between 1995 and 2012.
questions.explanation: Since the graph displays the rate of occupational growth, this means that the percentages presented in the graph are translated into the additional amount of people in a certain occupation. For example, a growth of 170% of Doctors is translated into an additional 170% doctors in 2012 on top of the 100% doctors working in their profession in 1995. questions.question:
Unemployment rate in 2012
*Master's degree and bachelor's degree are both university diplomas

Given the data in the graph, the number of unemployed people with only a high school diploma is 4/3 times the number of unemployed with a university diploma
questions.explanation: Although we do not know the exact size of the population of people who are eligible for work, we do know that the data given in the chart was extracted from the same population. Namely, all percentage data relates to the same whole and thus the percentages themselves can express the ratio between different categories without having to "translate" them into actual values. 12% (unemployed people with only a high school diploma) are 4/3 times as much as 4% + 5% = 9% (unemployed with a university diploma- bachelor's + masters degree). It doesn't really matter what the exact numbers are since it will always be true that the number of unemployed people with only a high school diploma will be 4/3 times the number of unemployed with a university diploma (because both categories relate to the same "whole").

questions.question:
Average Mental Performance Differences between Age Groups
Score range: 50-150

On average, men have higher IQ scores than women.
questions.explanation: The IQ scores of men and women are given in this question in average values. In order to compare the two averages, we need to take into account their weight in the distribution. In other words, we need to calculate the weighted average. The number of women in this experiment could be greater than the number of men (and vice versa),this would lead the average to incline more to the IQ of women rather than men because there are more of them. We are not given the distribution of the population so accordingly it's impossible to calculate the weighted average. Hence, the correct answer (C)-not possible to say.

Paris-Barcelona Daily Trains

The percentage of vacant seats on the 12 pm and 5pm trains is the same.
questions.explanation: Although the 12pm train has more vacant seats than the 5 pm train, when dealing with percentages one must remember that the relevant value(vacant seats) is always assessed in regards to the total value (total number of seats). Hence the greater number of vacant seats in the 12 pm train has no meaning without examining the total number of seats on that train: 12 pm train: 75/250= 0.3= 30% 5 pm train: 60/200= 0.3= 30% The percentage of vacant seats on the 12 pm and 5pm trains is the same.
